scope: P7 Sprint 2 batch — UTIL 5-table schema + 综合能耗 service (T0/T1/T2/T3/T4/T5)
summary: Reviewed 32 changed files. Found 1 P0 critical unit-conversion bug (steam/water toe_factor 1000x too small), 1 P0 zero-tolerance guard misses xls_reference with NULL total_toe, 1 P1 idempotent race, 1 P1 func.now() ORM-set may fail on SQLite, 2 P2 unit/tolerance edge cases, 1 P2 year-dimension mixing, 1 P2 default tolerance_status contradiction, and 1 pre-existing P3 in summary_service.

findings.title: Steam/Water toe_factor applied with t (tonne) inputs but factor defined per kg — totals 1000x too small
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:167 — `agg.steam_t_yr * s_toe` multiplies TONNES by toe_factor 0.0760
pcs-backend/app/models/config.py:1051-1056 — ConfigEnergyConversionFactor.toe_factor comment explicitly states `蒸汽=kg` (steam unit = kg) but `annual_consumption_t` is in tonnes/yr

pcs-backend/scripts/p7_open_009_t0_seed_energy_conversion_factors.py:64-66 — seed value 0.0760 annotated `kg 蒸汽 → kg 标油` and `76 kg 标油/t`; numerically 0.0760 kg/kg = 76 kg/t, but service applies it as if per-tonne (no ×1000 conversion of steam_t_yr)

pcs-backend/tests/services/util/fixtures/golden_utility_energy_summary.json:28 — T5_CASE_01_SMALL: 20,000 t steam → expected total_toe_tonne=14.0558 (≈ 1520 kg steam toe); a real refinery's annual steam gives tens of thousands of tonnes of toe — numbers confirm a 1000x undercount
Same unit bug applies to WATER: agg.water_t_yr * w_toe with w_toe=0.0001 (per kg, per model docstring) but water_t_yr is in t/yr; off by 1000x
findings.suggested_fix:
Pick one of two reconciliations:
  (A) Treat toe_factor as per-tonne for steam/water (matches service math) — update ConfigEnergyConversionFactor docstring (line 1027) and seed comment (line 65, 70) to explicitly state `蒸汽=t`、`水=t` instead of `=kg`. Confirm with工艺室 which unit GB/T 50441 appendix uses.
  (B) Treat toe_factor as per-kg (matches config model docstring) — change service to `agg.steam_t_yr * 1000 * s_toe` (and `* 1000 * w_toe` for water). Recompute golden fixture expected values (e.g., T5_CASE_01 total_toe_tonne should become ~14055.8 tonne, not 14.0558).
Either way, recalibrate golden_utility_energy_summary.json expected totals and re-run vitest. The unit inconsistency between model/seed/service is a foot-gun regardless of which side is canonical.

findings.title: tolerance_pct guard `xls_reference.total_toe > 0` raises TypeError when total_toe is None
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:236 — `if xls_reference is not None and xls_reference.total_toe > 0:`
model utility.py:465 — total_toe declared `nullable=False`, but service callers can construct an xls_reference ORM instance with total_toe unset → Python None; `None > 0` raises TypeError in CPython

test_utility_energy_summary.py:320 — the test happens to set `annual_total_energy=0.0` and `toe_conversion_factor=1e-9`, but `total_toe` defaults to NOT NULL default per ORM, so the path isn't covered
If xls_reference row is committed via raw SQL or partial inserts (e.g., bulk import future), total_toe may be NULL, breaking the service call
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:236 — `if xls_reference is not None and xls_reference.total_toe > 0:`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `and xls_reference.total_toe > 0` with `and xls_reference.total_toe is not None and xls_reference.total_toe > 0`. Or use a helper: `xls_reference_total_toe = (xls_reference.total_toe or 0.0) if xls_reference is not None else None`.

findings.title: Idempotent update has TOCTOU race: two concurrent summarize calls both miss existing row and one fails IntegrityError
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:245-253 — non-locking SELECT for existing row, then INSERT-or-UPDATE outside any transaction isolation
model util.py:399-403 — UNIQUE(project_id, business_year, source) will reject the second concurrent INSERT
AsyncSession default isolation is READ COMMITTED in PG; the SELECT-UPDATE gap allows a duplicate INSERT that violates UNIQUE
Endpoint POST /energy-summary/aggregate does not wrap in a transaction or use SELECT FOR UPDATE
No retry / IntegrityError handler — caller gets an opaque 500 instead of a clean idempotent overwrite
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:245-253 — non-locking SELECT then INSERT-or-UPDATE without transaction wrap
findings.suggested_fix:
Either:
  (A) Use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (project_id, business_year, source) DO UPDATE SET ...` raw SQL (PG-specific upsert).
  (B) Catch IntegrityError, re-query for existing, and apply the UPDATE branch.
  (C) Wrap SELECT + INSERT in a single SERIALIZABLE transaction.
Recommend (A) for atomicity; (B) is portable but racy.

findings.title: ORM-set `existing.computed_at = func.now()` may execute as raw SQL in UPDATE on PostgreSQL but fail on SQLite (test backend)
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:270 — `existing.computed_at = func.now()`
Migration p7_open_009_005_utility_energy_summary.py:170-175 — `computed_at` column has `server_default=sa.func.now()` which fires only on INSERT; explicit assignment is required for UPDATE
SQLAlchemy 2.x may serialize `func.now()` as a literal SQL expression in UPDATE for PG; SQLite via aiosqlite may render it as a bound parameter and error with `no such function: now`
Tests run on SQLite in-memory per test docstring; idempotent test calls summarize_energy_year twice and expects 2nd call to succeed — if SQLite rejects, the test would fail
findings.suggested_fix: Use a Python-side datetime: `existing.computed_at = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)`. Or define `onupdate=func.now()` on the ORM column (line 489 already has `onupdate=func.now()`!) — but the column attribute is then ALSO explicitly set in code, defeating the onupdate. Either remove the explicit line OR keep onupdate and rely on it; do not set both.

findings.title: T5 service writes water_t_yr / gas_nm3_yr / low_temp_heat_gj_yr as 0.0 even though they are nullable
evidence: model util.py:441-452 — water_t_yr / gas_nm3_yr / low_temp_heat_gj_yr all declared nullable=True with comments `待 P7-6B 落地 / 预留字段`
service util.py:260-262, 281-283 — writes 0.0 literal instead of None, conflating 'aggregated and equals zero' with 'no source data yet'

Per SERVICE-COMMENT line 67-69 `cooling_water / gas / low_temp_heat 子表待 P7-6B 落地, 当前返回 0.0`, but those three are explicitly marked nullable in model — 0.0 makes them indistinguishable from real zero-consumption projects
Downstream queries like `WHERE water_t_yr IS NULL` to find projects awaiting cooling-water aggregation will return empty set
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:260-262 — writes 0.0 for nullable fields awaiting P7-6B
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep 0.0 and document the convention (drop nullable), OR write NULL when the source subtable is empty. Recommended: write NULL until the corresponding subtable exists; the `annual_total_energy` and `total_toe` formulas already tolerate 0/NULL inputs.

findings.title: T5 service ignores `business_year` when aggregating T1/T2/T3 — projects with multi-year data will mix years
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:62-68 — `_aggregate_util_subtables` explicitly says `business_year 当前未用于过滤 (T1/T2/T3 表无 year 字段; 数据为 project snapshot); 预留接口`
models util.py:421-424 — UtilityEnergySummary.business_year is non-null Integer with comment `业务年度 ... annual aggregation`
models util.py:115-191 / 194-279 / 281-377 — UtilityPowerItem / UtilityFuelGas / UtilityHeatExchange have NO year column; aggregation always picks all rows for project_id
If T1 data is recorded for year 2025 and 2026 in the same project, calling summarize for business_year=2026 will sum both years' annual_consumption_kwh — wrong
Docstring acknowledges this as 'snapshot'; consider whether this is intentional or a hidden semantic footgun
findings.suggested_fix: Add `business_year` column to T1/T2/T3 tables OR enforce in service that only one year's worth of subtable rows may exist per project_id. For Sprint 2 minimum, document the snapshot assumption in API docs and add a CHECK that warns when subtable rows were created across multiple years for the same project.

findings.title: tolerance_status default conflict: ORM server_default='OK' but service initial value is 'NA'
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:234-235 — `tolerance_pct: float | None = None; tolerance_status = "NA"` initialised when xls_reference is None
model util.py:478 — `tolerance_status: ... server_default="OK"` — server default is 'OK', service code path is 'NA'
Migration ck constraint L210 enforces tolerance_status IN ('OK', 'EXCEEDED', 'NA') — both literals are valid

Service-vs-server-default divergence: if service ever constructs UtilityEnergySummary directly without populating tolerance_status, ORM applies server_default 'OK'; service path always overrides to 'NA' then potentially 'OK'/'EXCEEDED' — confusing for any caller that reads raw attribute before commit

API endpoint aggregate_energy_summary never passes xls_reference → all freshly-created rows have tolerance_status='NA' (fine) but server_default in any direct INSERT via raw SQL would set 'OK' (inconsistent with API behavior)
findings.suggested_fix: Align server_default with service semantics: change server_default from `"OK"` to `"NA"` in util.py:478 (and migration L166). Document the semantic: NA means no XLS reference yet.

findings.title: _compute_totals unit constants (KWH_TO_MJ, NM3_FUEL_GAS_TO_MJ, T_STEAM_TO_MJ, GJ_LOW_TEMP_TO_MJ) are hardcoded with TODO — values diverge from per-unit toe_factor semantics
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/utility_energy_summary_service.py:134-139 — `KWH_TO_MJ = 3.6`, `NM3_FUEL_GAS_TO_MJ = 38.0`, `T_STEAM_TO_MJ = 2778.0`, `GJ_LOW_TEMP_TO_MJ = 1000.0`
Comment L123-129 says `(简化假设; 待 P7-6B 工艺室精化)` — these are placeholder simplifications, not authoritative values

2778 MJ/t for 1 MPa saturated steam implies 66 kg 标油/t at standard TOE conversion (1 toe = 41.868 GJ), but toe_factor seeded as 0.076 kg/kg = 76 kg/t — internal inconsistency between MJ-total and toe-total derivations

Cruise 38 MJ/Nm³ for fuel gas is a 'typical LHV' but real calorific_value_kcal_nm3 is recorded per-row in T2 (model util.py:247-250) and is NEVER used by the service — fuel_gas_mj assumes 38 MJ/Nm³ universally, ignoring recorded calorific_value

annual_total_energy computed from these constants differs from total_toe/coal-derived totals; the formula `toe_conversion_factor = total_toe*1000/annual_total_energy` produces a derived factor that mixes the two assumptions
findings.suggested_fix:
(A) Compute energy MJ from per-row calorific_value when available: `fuel_gas_mj = sum(annual_consumption_nm3 * calorific_value_kcal_nm3 * 4.1868 / 1000)` (kcal→kJ conversion: 4.1868 kJ/kcal; divide by 1000 for MJ).
(B) For steam, compute MJ from steam quality × latent heat + sensible heat: `steam_mj = annual_consumption_t * 1000 * (steam_quality_pct/100 * latent_heat_kj_kg + sensible_heat_kj_per_kg) / 1000`.
(C) Until P7-6B delivers authoritative values, document current constants as 'assumption-based' and add a per-input bypass in service signature.

findings.title: summary_service.summarize computes toe_total/standard_coal_total for STEAM categories without unit conversion (t/h × per-kg factor)
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/util/summary_service.py:91-92 — `toe_total += qty * float(toe_row.toe_conversion_factor)` and `standard_coal_total += qty * float(toe_row.standard_coal_factor)`
category_map.py:44-58 — STEAM_HP/MP/LP + CONDENSATE units are `t/h`
config_domain.py:342-344 — ToeConversionFactor.toe_conversion_factor/standard_coal_factor units are unitless multipliers (unspecified)
Pre-existing service (not modified by Sprint 2); ambiguous unit interpretation likely matches 13-class legacy convention where t/h is treated as nominal — flag for review but mark pre_existing
findings.suggested_fix: Out of scope for Sprint 2; flag in TODOS.md for follow-up. Verify with 工艺室 whether STEAM TOE is per-tonne or per-kg; align with the new ConfigEnergyConversionFactor model decisions.

residual_risks: P0 unit bug (steam/water 1000x): if shipped, all 综合能耗 reports will be 0.1% of real numbers and tolerance vs XLS_REFERENCE will always show EXCEEDED — UI dashboards will break.
Race condition: high concurrency on POST /energy-summary/aggregate (e.g., nightly batch) will produce intermittent IntegrityError 500s.

NaN compat for CHECK constraints: PostgreSQL evaluates NaN comparisons as NULL → INSERT violates NOT NULL/CHECK if total_toe / annual_total_energy ever becomes NaN. The service currently can't produce NaN from finite float inputs, but if DB returns NaN (impossible for Float type) it would slip through.
func.now() in ORM attribute assignment on SQLite: if SQLite is used for any production deployment, idempotent update path will fail.
Year-dimension mixing: a project with multi-year equipment data will silently aggregate across years.

GET /util/summary and GET /util/energy-consumption still read from UtilResults.consumption_json (13-class JSONB) via summary_service.summarize, NOT from the new 5-table aggregation. After Sprint 2 the JSONB path and the 5-table path produce DIFFERENT toe_total numbers for the same project — consumers don't know which to trust.
testing_gaps: No test for tolerance_pct with xls_reference.total_toe = None (NoneType vs 0.0 vs positive).
No test for concurrent summarize calls — race window untested.

Golden fixture expected values are computed by hand-derivation from the buggy service; they will pass tests even if the bug exists. No independent cross-check against GB/T 50441 appendix or工艺室-computed 外部估计.
API tests in test_util_sprint2.py only cover zero-consumption path; no test asserts total_toe > 0 after a single T1 row insert via API → the 1000x bug would not surface from API tests.
No test for `existing.computed_at = func.now()` SQLite compat — if tests run on PG only (not SQLite), the bug won't surface in CI.
No test verifies the JSONB-vs-5-table dual paths produce consistent totals for the same project data.
No test for water/gas/low_temp_heat None-vs-0 semantics; consumers can't tell aggregated-zero from not-yet-aggregated.
summary_service tests don't verify STEAM unit conversion with hand-calculated MJ total.

reviewer_notes.primary_tier_scope: All 32 changed files reviewed; hot paths: utility_energy_summary_service.py, util.py (api/v1), util.py (models), 6 alembic versions, util.py (schemas), config.py (ConfigEnergyConversionFactor).
reviewer_notes.secondary_scope: summary_service.py toe calculation used by existing 13-class JSONB path.
reviewer_notes.pre_existing_flag: summary_service.py:91 unit ambiguity is pre-existing (Sprint 1) and not modified by Sprint 2 — flagged pre_existing: true.
reviewer_notes.false_positives_avoided: Idempotent update IS a real race but practical probability is low; flagged P1 not P0.
reviewer_notes.tests_passing_due_to_compounding_bugs: Golden fixture Case 1 computes 20000 t × 0.0760 = 1520 kg — only correct if factor is per-tonne, not per-kg. Either the model docstring is wrong or the service is wrong; fixture follows service. Tests pass either way (wrong-on-both-sides).
